post.title: Dry Rot Repair Lake Stevens WA — Finding Hidden Decay, Permits, Flashing and Lasting Repairs
post.description: A Lake Stevens guide to dry rot repair: where decay hides, how to probe and measure moisture, why the water source comes first, when City permits apply, and the flashing and clearance details that make a repair last.

notes: Box-authored fallback. Home PC DESKTOP-B69F181 connected but board-intake inbox had no 2026-11-15 packets at 3:47 AM PT; PC not touched. Topic: dry rot repair in Lake Stevens WA (Snohomish County). Where decay hides (corner trim, fascia, sills, rim joist/sill plate, deck ledger, bath subfloor); probing, moisture meters, opening up; water source first (EPA mold/moisture guide, dry within 24-48 h); FS Wood Handbook. City of Lake Stevens: Planning and Community Development 1812 Main St, (425) 622-9400, permits@; Citizens Connect portal; Ordinance 1160 adds R105.2 exemptions 11 (lightweight reroof <4 psf) and 12 (windows in existing openings); Residential Interior Permit Exemptions sheet (siding repair/replacement, trim, windows in existing openings, painting, drywall holes; exemption doesn't authorize code violations); Residential Inspections Handout (no concealment before approval, weather barrier/window flashing inspection, electrical via L&I); Deck Tip Sheet (permit if >=200 sf, >=30 in, attached, or required exit; PT or decay-resistant wood, end cut solution, SS/HDG fasteners; engineer for ledger over bay windows/brick/stone/CMU, hot tub); owner-builder form (RCW 18.27, city business license). IRC 2021 ch.3 decay protection (8 in framing on foundation; 6 in siding/sheathing/framing to ground, 2 in to slabs) and ch.7 flashing (shingle-fashion at windows/doors, projecting trim, deck attachment); WA adoption 51-51 WAC.
